LESSON: READING 8.2.1 INTENSIVE READING – LEGENDS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.2: Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do you read intensively?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. respond to questions from legends for comprehension

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 8.2.1 INTENSIVE READING – LEGENDS
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 9
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 8.2.1 INTENSIVE READING – LEGENDS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Respond to questions from legends for comprehension

What this means
In this part you learn to respond to questions from legends for comprehension. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: respond to questions from legends for comprehension.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can respond to questions from legends for comprehension. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: respond to questions from legends for comprehension)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: respond to questions from legends for comprehension.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 9 learner study Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do you read intensively?
2. Why can an individual be considered a legend in the society?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 8.2.1 Intensive Reading – Legends means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: respond to questions from legends for comprehension.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
